finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") but ignores its boolean return value, so the OWNER check never blocks execution and any caller can wipe any tenant (if the route is reachable by non-OWNER users).
finding.source: tenant path parameter and caller User record passed into wipe(User u, String tenant), POST /tenants/{t}/wipe (src/Admin.java:24-25)
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, destructive tenant-wide operation

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) entry point
requireRole(u, "OWNER") called; result discarded, no throw or return
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) as a boolean and does not throw

finding.guards_checked: Only guard in this file is requireRole at line 26, which is non-enforcing. export() at line 32 uses checkRole, which throws, and is correct. No caller, auth middleware, or role-loading code is in the repo, so route reachability by unprivileged users is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: Admin.java:26 requireRole(u, "OWNER") is a bare statement whose boolean result is discarded, so it enforces nothing; Admin.java:14-15 confirms it only returns a boolean and never throws. checkRole at Admin.java:18-22 throws but is not called by wipe(). No other guard exists in the repo (only src/Admin.java is present).
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: requireRole at src/Admin.java:26 returns a boolean that is discarded, so repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 runs for any caller that reaches wipe(). Whether a non-OWNER user can reach it is undecidable here, because the POST route wiring, auth middleware, and role loading are not in the repo, so an upstream guard could still block it.

finding.claim: Roles are global (User has no tenant or membership field), and checkRole only tests whether OWNER is in the global set, so an OWNER of tenant A can export tenant B.
finding.source: tenant path parameter in export(User u, String tenant) (src/Admin.java:30-31), POST /tenants/{t}/export
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33, exports tenant data

trace.note: User record has only name and global roles set, no tenant scope
export(User u, String tenant) entry point, tenant from URL
checkRole(u, "OWNER") checks global role only, not membership in tenant
repo.export(tenant) runs for any tenant id supplied

finding.guards_checked: checkRole throws correctly on missing role, but nothing binds the caller to the target tenant in this file. Tenant-membership enforcement could exist in the caller or in Repo, which is not in the repo. Confidence depends on whether roles are intended to be global.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole at src/Admin.java:18-22 is a real throwing guard, but it only tests the global role set and never binds the caller to the target tenant. No tenant-membership check exists in src/Admin.java:31-33. The Repo implementation and the HTTP/router layer are not in the repo (Glob returns only src/Admin.java), so an upstream tenant check cannot be ruled out.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: User has only name and roles (src/Admin.java:4), checkRole at line 32 checks only the global OWNER role, and repo.export(tenant) runs unchecked at line 33. Whether a tenant-owner can reach another tenant's export depends on the Repo implementation and the request router, neither of which is in the repo, so the finding can be neither confirmed nor refuted from this code. Separately, src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole, which returns a bool that is discarded, so wipe() at line 27 runs for any user; that is a stronger and separate defect worth reporting on its own.
